world.label: Pencil Supply Chain
world.summary: Specialists make, move, and sell pencils through a supply chain that keeps producing and replenishing shop stock.

actions.description: Cut cedar into logs.
The mill buys logs from the logging crew.
Saw logs into cedar slats.
Mine graphite.
The lead maker buys graphite from the mine.
Mix graphite with clay and form pencil leads.
The pencil factory buys cedar slats from the mill.
The pencil factory buys leads from the lead maker.
Glue leads into slats, paint the pencils, and add erasers and brass ferrules.
Pack finished pencils into boxes.
The trucking company delivers packed pencil boxes from the factory to a shop.
A shop sells pencils to a customer and receives payment.
A shop adds to its count of pencils waiting to be replenished.

readout.title: How goods moved through the chain
readout.summary: The logger and graphite mine replenished raw materials, while the sawmill made slats, the lead-maker made leads, and the pencil factory assembled and packed pencils. Goods moved between businesses and the shop repeatedly sold pencils to customers; no step is shown waiting for missing supplies.

mechanisms.name: Goods made from other goods
mechanisms.explanation: The lead-maker used clay and graphite to make leads, the pencil factory used components to assemble pencils and packed pencils, and the sawmill used logs to make slats.

mechanisms.name: Goods carried to the next step
mechanisms.explanation: Leads, logs, graphite, and slats moved between businesses for later production. The trucking company also took packed pencils from the pencil factory as part of delivery.

mechanisms.name: Demand reached and met
mechanisms.explanation: Customers bought pencils from the shop, gaining pencils while the shop's stock fell. These sales met customer demand.
